findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. Fix name selection at src/forge/task.py:336–341 considers branches and merged state, but not retained tags. After removing an unmerged branch and worktree, restarting its slug creates and commits a new checkout before this create-only update-ref fails on the existing tag. Story and task name reuse have the same failure; copied-plan tasks can fail earlier on the forge-plan tag at line 123. Check or reserve both retained tag names before creating work, preserving the original references.
findings.title: Account for retained tags before reusing an abandoned branch name

findings.body: A Tasks row with a backtick-formatted ID such as `SAVE` is accepted and normalized by src/forge/story.py:362–374, but task.rows preserves the raw ID at src/forge/task.py:53–62. When that row has a Developer, this loop passes SHOP/`SAVE` to row(), which calls repo.state_path and refuses the invalid item (src/forge/repo.py:635–639). The human board has the same problem at board.py:569–572. Both board commands therefore fail for an accepted assigned plan. Normalize IDs before synthetic-row creation and assignment lookup in both board paths.
findings.title: Normalize task IDs before adding assigned board rows

findings.body: For forge story new --from-fix, src/forge/story.py:905–912 renames the fix branch and moves its state into the first task in a commit named “Turn the fix into the first part of its story”. This new attribution query excludes that commit because it only matches Start messages, while the original start commit records only the old fix-state path. Consequently, the promoted part has started_by=null on both boards, including after close and cleanup. Preserve the association with the original fix starter when promotion changes the item's path.
findings.title: Preserve starter attribution when promoting a fix into a story part

findings.body: The previous P2 remains open. The selected published plan is read here, but approval is checked only through approval.waiting_digest(key, path) at nextstep.py:419. A teammate without a local story worktree skips that check entirely; a stale local worktree can also check its old plan instead of the selected published plan. If the published plan has a passing cold read but lacks approval or awaits renewed approval, next offers assigned parts as able to start, while task start refuses them at src/forge/task.py:241–245. Validate the selected state's approval hash against the reconciled text before offering starts.
findings.title: Check approval before offering starts from a published draft

findings.body: For an ongoing story, a merged assigned part older than seven days is omitted from children by board.py:413–414 and the expiry calculation at board.py:620–635. This loop then treats its absence as evidence that it never started, recreates it, and unconditionally overrides its stage to unstarted—even though row() detects its merged state. Both board --json and next --json consequently resurrect archived completed work as unstarted assignments. Check merged/expired state before synthesizing an unstarted row.
findings.title: Do not recreate expired merged assignments as unstarted parts

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow (2026-10-09): keep who started an item through a stacked fix replayed onto the default branch and through a story's first part that starts from the default branch and copies the plan, with a test for each; nothing else changes.

why: On a team, started work stays on the laptop where it began until its first close, so teammates can't see who is working on what and two developers can start the same part; no person is shown on any item. Owner decision 2026-10-09: starting is the claim, with git as the one record
